blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Waterfall — Primarily sequential software-development life cycle.
Agile — Iterative approach using feedback and incremental releases.
XP — Extreme Programming, an agile methodology with disciplined engineering practices.
test-driven development — Write an automated test before writing the production behaviour.

blocks.title: Waterfall is sequential
blocks.text: Agree requirements, then design, implementation, testing and deployment. Revisiting an earlier stage can be costly.

blocks.title: Agile delivers incrementally
blocks.text: Each short iteration produces working software and seeks feedback, so priorities can change between iterations.

blocks.title: Extreme Programming (XP)
blocks.text: XP is an agile methodology emphasising practices such as test-driven development, pair programming, refactoring and continuous integration.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: Requirements and approval milestones can be documented before later stages proceed.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model and explain
blocks.text: Waterfall offers clear documentation and control, but late changes can require expensive rework.
